title: Human-in-the-Loop Agent Workflows
description: Implement approval gates, user overrides, and intervention points in autonomous agent workflows for enterprise safety.

data.text: Fully autonomous agents are powerful but risky in enterprise settings. Human-in-the-loop (HITL) workflows insert deliberate checkpoints where humans review, approve, or override agent decisions. The key is designing these checkpoints to be minimally disruptive to the user experience while maximizing safety for critical operations like financial transactions, data access, or external API calls.

data.caption: Human-in-the-loop agent decision flow with approval gates
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    Start([User Request]) --> Analyze[Agent Analysis]
    Analyze --> RiskAssessment{Risk Level}
    RiskAssessment -->|Low| Execute[Auto-execute Action]
    RiskAssessment -->|Medium| Pause[Pause & Request Approval]
    RiskAssessment -->|High| Escalate[Escalate to Human]
    Pause --> HumanApprove{Human Approves?}
    HumanApprove -->|Yes| Execute
    HumanApprove -->|No| Revise[Revise Plan]
    Revise --> Analyze
    Execute --> Result[Action Result]
    Result --> Continue{More Steps?}
    Continue -->|Yes| Analyze
    Continue -->|No| Complete[Return to User]

data.text: Approval gates intercept agent tool calls and require human confirmation before execution. They are classified by risk: financial gates (amount thresholds), data access gates (PII, compliance), destructive gates (deletion, modification), and external API gates (third-party calls).

data.text: Intervention allows a human to step into an ongoing agent session. Unlike approval gates (which block before execution), intervention occurs during execution. Common patterns: pausing the agent loop, modifying the agent's goals or instructions, providing direct tool calls, or resetting the conversation to a checkpoint.

data.text: Always log HITL decisions — approvals, interventions, and overrides — to an immutable audit log with timestamps, user IDs, and reasons. This is not optional for regulated industries.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Approval gates intercept tool calls based on risk classification (financial, data, destructive, external)
Intervention allows human modification of ongoing agent sessions via pause/override
All HITL decisions must be logged to immutable audit trails
Signal the agent's state changes to connected clients in real-time (SignalR)
Design approval flows to be friction-minimized but risk-maximized — block high-risk, auto-approve low-risk
data.takeaway: Human-in-the-loop is not a constraint on autonomy — it's a safety infrastructure layer that enables autonomous agents to operate in high-stakes environments.
